title: Shift coda — technical sketch and ad-hoc runbook
content:
Purpose: quick, minimal steps for the twilight/on-call handoff. This is not the canonical runbook — it's a scratch draft of things I did tonight and short-term mitigations that should be codified or replaced.

High-level summary of last 8h:
- Two partial degradations observed between 03:10-03:27 UTC: elevated tail latency for text-generation endpoints and a handful of 504s from the edge LB. Root cause hypothesis: sustained long-context requests triggered KV-cache churn + one autoscaler mis-evaluation that temporarily reduced worker concurrency on the p4po pool.
- Mitigations applied: increased worker_min to 6 for p4po (temporary), rolled traffic off the primary low-latency model to a smaller fallback model for requests > 4096 tokens, and purged stale prefixes in prefix-cache for customer-tenant: cust-873.
- User impact: intermittent 1–3s extra latency for ~4% of requests; error spike for one customer (cust-873) where requests hit 503. Customer success notified.

Open items to hand off:
1) Incident INF-4721 (see linked JIRA) — tracking follow-up on autoscaler heuristics and long-context policy.
2) Prefix cache leak suspicion — need to instrument size-by-tenant and add eviction events to trace. I left a temporary metric on the metrics namespace: serving.prefix_cache_size_temp (panel in my personal Grafana).
3) Short-term rollback of model v2.7 -> v2.6 for canary group B scheduled if latency climbs > 1s for 5 continuous minutes.

Immediate runbook (emergency short steps)
- Communication: post update in #eng-oncall and #prod-ops. Tag @oncall and @platform-lead.
- If tail latency > 1.5s for 3 minutes or 5xx rate > 1%: 1) scale worker pool, 2) reroute heavy-context trafic, 3) notify CS.

Quick commands / shortcuts (copy-paste friendly):
- Check autoscaler state (k8s): kubectl -n serving get hpa,pods -l pool=p4po -o wide
- Scale min workers (temporary): kubectl -n serving patch hpa p4po-worker --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":6}]'
- Roll traffic to fallback model via routing API:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
   https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/override \
   -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","target_model":"titan-fallback-quant","match":{"max_prompt_tokens":4096}}'
- Purge tenant prefix cache (redis): redis-cli -h prefix-cache.prod.redwood -n 2 --scan --pattern "tenant:cust-873:*" | xargs -L 100 redis-cli -h prefix-cache.prod.redwood -n 2 del
- Tail proxied logs (fluentd): kubectl -n infra logs -l app=fluentd --since=30m | grep "503" -C 4
- Sentry quick-link: https://sentry.redwood.io/organizations/redwood/issues/?project=serving
- Check trace for a sample request: go to tracing.redwood.io, set traceId from request header x-request-id

What I actually did tonight (note form):
- Noticed latency increase on grafana panel "serving.request.p50/p95 by pool" around 03:05 UTC.
- Looked at pod memory + KV hit ratio -> p4po pods were at ~78% mem and KV cache hit rate dropped from 0.92 -> 0.81 for the tenant in question.
- Increased worker_min to 6 and temporarily disabled aggressive batching (set BATCH_MAX_LATENCY_MS to 30) for p4po via configmap override.
- Rolled traffic for requests > 4096 tokens to titan-fallback-quant for 15 minutes.
- Watched errors subside; restarted one pod (p4po-5) after it accumulated 3 OOM Kills in 12h (kubectl delete pod p4po-5 -> new pod came up healthy).

Notes-to-self (immediately actionable)
- Add a taggable metric for "prefix-cache-kevictions" (kevictions = cache evictions events — yes the typo is intentional for local search) so we can correlate with OOM.
- Capture a heap-dump when pod mem > 85% for > 10 minutes (manual for now).
- Add a canary rule to limit long-context requests per tenant (soft-limit with 429 + guidance) — customers sending 10x above expected tail usage.

Escalation / contact matrix (short)
- On-call SRE (primary): @maya (PagerDuty)
- Senior SRE backup: Ravi Patel (Slack: @ravi, mobile: +1-415-555-0138)
- Platform lead: Ava Martinez (Slack: @ava)
- Product owner for hosting: Priyanka Rao (Slack: @priya)

What to include in the formal runbook (post-hand-off todo)
- Clear decision tree for long-context request handling: when to route, when to reject, and when to autoscale.
- Permanent autoscaler tuning: remove the 90s smoothing for downscales for pools with bursty inference.
- Concrete rollout / rollback checklist for model upgrades (v2.7 -> v2.6). Include exact traffic split commands and how to force full rollback.
- Add playbook subsection "prefix-cache troubleshooting" with: metrics to look at, sample Redis queries, how to compute per-tenant memory usage, and eviction remediation.

Outstanding questions / unknowns (to discuss in morning async thread):
- Why did the HPA decide to downscale during a rising queue? Check controller logs and the metric source (custom metrics adapter). Possible race with scaling cooldown.
- Are we double-counting tokens in the KV cache size metric? Instrumentation change requested.
- Should default fallback for long-context be served on CPU-only nodes to save GPU cycles? Pros/cons and cost impact.

Random thoughts / ideas (brainstorm)
- Lightweight "token budget" system for tenants: impose an optional billing-controllable guardrail that applies soft limits before traffic hits the main serving pool.
- Prefix-cache compaction job: run nightly for inactive tenants and snapshot frequently-used prefixes to fast-lookup storage.

Follow-ups I left as tickets:
- INF-4722: add prefix_cache_evictions metric + Grafana panel (assigned to @ravi)
- INF-4723: autoscaler tuning experiment doc + rollout plan (assigned to me)
- INF-4724: model rollback runbook draft + CLI snippets (assigned to @ava)

Closing notes to next on-call: leave me a note in this doc with what you changed and why. If you reroute traffic, please include start/stop timestamps and revert commands. This doc is thin and messy — it's intended to be ephemeral. If you find a pattern repeatable more than twice, open a proper runbook PR in the infra runbooks repo.

-- maya
plain_text_preview: Short: increased workers, routed long-context to fallback, purged tenant prefix cache, watching autoscaler behavior. TODOs: add eviction metric, tune autoscaler, crate rollback doc.
